Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM), as recommended by the American Diabetes Association (ADA), plays a critical role in the prevention of hypoglycemia, particularly in individuals receiving insulin therapy. This is especially true for those on intensive insulin regimens or using continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion systems. CGM technology is capable of identifying hypoglycemic events that occur without noticeable symptoms, enabling timely interventions to avert severe hypoglycemic episodes. Real-time CGM devices are especially advantageous because they are equipped with alarm systems that alert users to declining glucose levels, allowing them to take corrective action before severe hypoglycemic symptoms manifest.
